title: Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, reservations

kcs.statement: A Dedicated Host is a whole physical server for your use with visibility of its sockets and cores, chosen to bring per-socket or per-core software licenses (BYOL) or meet strict compliance rules; it is the most expensive EC2 option.
Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to one AWS account but give no visibility or control over the physical host, so they cannot satisfy server-bound licensing.

On-Demand Capacity Reservations guarantee EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for any duration and are billed at On-Demand rates whether used or not; they give no discount unless combined with Savings Plans or Regional RIs.

problem_ideas: A company owns per-core Windows Server and SQL Server licenses it wants to reuse: which EC2 option?
A regulator requires that no other customer shares the hardware but licensing is not server-bound: Dedicated Instance or Dedicated Host?
A retailer needs guaranteed capacity in one AZ for a 3-day Black Friday event without a 1-year term: which option?
